Pablo Picasso. From 1881 to 1973, a Spanish painter and sculptor who became the most influential artist of the twentieth century. Co-founder of Cubism and a master of multiple artistic styles from his melancholic Blue Period to Surrealism to Abstract Expressionism, Picasso fundamentally changed how art could represent reality. His prolific output, political activism, and restless innovation made him synonymous with modernism itself and the radical rupture between representational and non-representational art.

Picasso's genius lay not in perfecting a single style but in inventing styles wholesale and then moving beyond them. He lived through the century's greatest upheavals, Modernism, world wars, and fascism, and his art reflected that turbulence. Guernica became the twentieth century's most powerful anti-war statement. His willingness to fragment, distort, and reimagine the human figure opened the door to all modern and contemporary art that followed.

Born in Málaga, Spain in 1881, Picasso showed prodigious artistic talent from childhood and trained classically under his father, a painter and professor. He created works in the Blue Period from 1901 to 1904, painting melancholic figures in predominantly blue tones, poor, suffering, and isolated subjects, reflecting his own early struggles in Paris.

Picasso co-founded Cubism around 1907, along with Georges Braque, fragmenting objects into geometric planes and showing them from multiple viewpoints simultaneously, dismantling centuries of single-point perspective. He painted Les Demoiselles d'Avignon in 1907, depicting five nude female figures with flattened, distorted bodies and clashing colors, a manifesto work that shocked Paris and inaugurated Cubism.

He developed Analytical Cubism from 1908 to 1912, reducing objects to near-abstract arrangements of planes and facets, and Synthetic Cubism, reintroducing color and collage elements. Picasso created Guernica in 1937, a massive mural painting depicting the bombing of the Basque town of Guernica during the Spanish Civil War, a raw, fragmented cry against violence that remains modernism's greatest political artwork.

He worked extensively in sculpture, ceramics, and printmaking. His sculptural works pioneered assemblage and the use of found objects as art. Picasso passed through Surrealist and Neoclassical phases, constantly reinventing his approach while maintaining his distinctive, instantly recognizable artistic voice. He maintained a fraught romantic life, often painting his partners including Françoise Gilot and Dora Maar. Many of his works are intimate chronicles of desire, jealousy, and possession.

Picasso lived to age 91, producing over 50,000 works including paintings, sculptures, prints, and ceramics, making him one of the most prolific artists in history.
